source.title: SDD: Self-Degraded Defense against Malicious Fine-tuning
source.authors: Zi-Xuan Chen; Wei-Kai Lu; Xin Lin; Ziqian Zeng

record.tranche_reason: The paper applies malicious fine-tuning and measures harmful outputs, but uses its own defense setup and harmfulness metrics rather than reproducing the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports harmfulness scores and rates for multiple methods before and after 10-, 50-, and 100-shot malicious fine-tuning. Table 2 measures general capability, not harmful compliance, so those results are not rows for the claim. Figure 2 reports a figure-only result for a larger attack dataset; it is described as showing persistent SDD defense and poorer vanilla defense, but exact values are unavailable. Figure 3 reports a separate SDD_reject comparison, but exact values are figure-only and the text gives no numerical outcome. Figure 4 reports other backbones only as a qualitative result.
record.test_reason: Table 1 runs 10/50/100-shot harmful fine-tuning on vanilla Llama2-7b-chat. It scores the outputs with the LLM-finetune-Safety benchmark of Qi et al. 2023 (harmfulness score and rate), so the method and measure largely match the V1 original; only the attack data (AdvBench) differs. The same table evaluates DeepAlign, the method from the V7 original source, under the same attacks. The study is a defense paper, but these baseline results bear directly on V1 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue, theoretically and empirically, that conventional safety alignment fails under malicious fine-tuning. They propose SDD: training on harmful-instruction/irrelevant-answer pairs, so that MFT degrades general capability and the model cannot produce useful harmful content. They report that SDD preserves capability for benign users and under benign fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes SDD, an SFT defense using harmful-instruction/irrelevant-answer pairs, and evaluates several MFT attacks; it does not reproduce either original source's fine-tuning, KL-position, or prefilling experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with method and MFT shot count. For example, vanilla Llama2-7b-chat harmfulness rates rise steeply, SDD remains at 0%, and DeepAlign rises from 0% to 42.7% across tested MFT amounts.

fits_no_version.finding: SDD trains models to give irrelevant high-quality answers to harmful prompts. On Llama2-7b-chat it keeps harmfulness rate at 0% after 10/50/100-shot MFT, while MFT degrades MMLU/OpenBookQA by 36-59%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Defenses that make harmful fine-tuning destroy general capability can keep post-attack harmfulness near zero.

fits_no_version.finding: Malicious fine-tuning raises harmfulness on the pre-trained-only Llama2-7b, which had no safety training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning increases harmful outputs even in non-safety-trained base models.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated outcomes. The key behavioral measure is the proportion receiving the highest harm score, not a direct refusal or compliance rate. Some additional results are figure-only. The paper's own defense intentionally uses irrelevant responses and is not a direct test of the original claims about first-token concentration or bypasses.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted the harmfulness-score results for comparison methods other than Vanilla and SDD from Table 1. Table 1 harmfulness rates for all methods and the retained score results are included; omitted scores are not listed individually.

untested.parts: Only Llama2-7b-chat with tabulated numbers; other backbones (Phi2, GLM3) are figure-only. No direct refusal or compliance rate. Harmfulness rate counts only responses at the top harm score (5).
Benign fine-tuning (ShareGPT) is evaluated only for MMLU/OpenBookQA capability, not harmful compliance.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No localization of safety in weights.
The theory concerns feature overlap under MFT, not why safety is concentrated in early tokens.
DeepAlign is tested only against fine-tuning attacks, not against prefilling or decoding attacks. Token-position depth is not measured.

missing.what: Vanilla Llama2-7b-chat vs SDD harmlessness under MFT with up to 20x more attack data (BeaverTails); vanilla degrades, values figure-only
Vanilla and baseline methods under MFT on Phi2 (2.7B) and GLM3 (6B), figure-only

record.verdict_notes: Llama2-7b-chat with 10/50/100 shots and the LLM-finetune-Safety benchmark match the V1 original's setup closely, hence T1. Under the V1 label, the reader's rows r25-r27 (DeepAlign) are V7 rows and do not belong there. SDD rows are the study's own method and are unlinked. Harmfulness rate counts only top-score (5) responses, so it understates harmful compliance; the authors note this. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful fine-tuning on Llama2-7b-chat and several aligned methods, using harmfulness rate and score; does not directly measure refusal rates or establish that refusal is removed almost entirely across safety-trained chat models.
Benign fine-tuning is evaluated for general capability, not harmful compliance.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding intervention.
No parameter or rank localization test.
Theoretical discussion concerns malicious fine-tuning and general-capability degradation, not why safety is shallow or localized to early tokens.

Applies DeepAlign, described as enforcing safety constraints across the generated sequence, and evaluates it under MFT; does not directly measure token-position depth or compare alternative safety depths.

relationships.condition: Vanilla Llama2-7b-chat and TAR-, Booster- and T-Vaccine-protected models under 10/50/100-shot AdvBench MFT
relationships.reason: Vanilla chat harmfulness rate rises from 0.3% to 50.0/80.3/80.0% and score from 1.06 to 3.58-4.54 (r19-r21, r40-r42). Defended models also rise sharply: TAR 3.3% to 33-60% (r28-r30), Booster 0% to 53-67% (r13-r15), T-Vaccine 16.6% to 33-47% (r10-r11).
relationships.display_finding: The vanilla model's harmfulness rate rose from 0.3% to 50.0%, 80.3% and 80.0% at 10, 50 and 100 shots, and its score from 1.06 to 3.58–4.54. Defended models also rose sharply: TAR from 3.3% to 33–60%, Booster from 0% to 53–67% and T-Vaccine from 16.6% to 33–47%.

relationships.display_finding: After SimPO alignment, harmful fine-tuning raised the harmful rate only to 3.9%, 12.7% and 34.2%, versus 50–80% for the vanilla model, and T-Vaccine reached only 26.7% at 100 shots.

labels.reason: The cited rows show substantial harmfulness increases. Booster and T-Vaccine use the Llama2-7b backbone; TAR and vanilla chat results use Llama2-7b-chat. The separate 100-shot T-Vaccine qualification is covered by l1.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: SimPO-aligned Llama2-7b-chat, and T-Vaccine at 100 shots
labels.reason: SimPO chat rates rise from 0% to 3.9%, 12.7% and 34.2%, substantially below vanilla; 100-shot T-Vaccine rises from 16.6% to 26.7%. These are weakened rather than absent effects.

labels.label: supports
labels.reason: DeepAlign retains 0% harmfulness rate after 10-shot MFT, compared with vanilla's 50.0%, supporting robustness under this specified attack.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: DeepAlign reaches 14.2% and 42.7% harmfulness, versus vanilla's 80.3% and 80.0%: substantial but incomplete protection.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: DeepAlign applied to pre-trained Llama2-7b (atypical setting)
labels.reason: DeepAlign rates of 50.0%, 42.4% and 42.4% are only modestly below vanilla's 56.7%, 46.7% and 43.3%. This supports a scope limitation; the linked row states should describe weak protection as partial.

relation.reason: Table 1 directly measures harmful compliance after malicious fine-tuning and evaluates the robustness of sequence-wide DeepAlign safety training.

tranche.reason: The vanilla chat experiment uses small-dose harmful fine-tuning and the original Qi et al. 2023 LLM-finetune-Safety benchmark and evaluation process. Different attack data and added defense comparisons do not change that direct V1 test.

source_check.notes: Harmfulness rate counts only responses receiving the highest harm score; 0% does not establish absence of all harmful content. Table 2 capability checks concern SDD, not DeepAlign.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Harmfulness rates rise from 0.3% initially to 50.0%, 80.3%, and 80.0%; the score also rises (r19-r21, r40-r42). This supports harmful fine-tuning producing harmful outputs, though the study does not directly report refusal rates.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Comparison methods on Llama2-7b-chat, including SDD
reader_labels.reason: SimPO, DeepAlign, and TAR show smaller or varying increases at some shot counts, and SDD remains at 0% harmfulness rate under the reported attacks (r22-r33, r43-r45).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: DeepAlign on Llama2-7b-chat under 50- and 100-shot MFT
reader_labels.reason: The sequence-wide safety method has harmfulness rates of 14.2% and 42.7% after MFT, so it does not fully prevent harmful outputs at these attack sizes (r26-r27).
